column1: # readme-archives.tsv — which SAMPLE ARCHIVES each published README cell is reduced from.
# Tab-separated, tracked. Added 2026-10-09 for #165, whose words are "pin the canonical sample
# archives per row in a manifest to close the log<->sample provenance ambiguity".
# WHY IT EXISTS, and it is not hypothetical. scripts/readme-numbers.sh takes GATE LOGS and
# reduces the SAMPLE FILES those logs name. The names it prints are "build/..." paths, which are
# gitignored, so on any fresh clone the stated provenance resolves to nothing and a reader must
# guess which archived copy a log meant. The guess has a wrong answer available: era pinned8
# archived TWO sample sets per host at rev 6ba6566 -- 20260823T004407Z (the canonical take, from
# campaign-c30-6ba6566.log) and 20260822T231901Z (a SUPERSEDED take, from campaign-6ba6566.log,
# whose zen5 Strsm/8 reads 427.1 and does not reproduce the published block). They differ only in
# a timestamp. On 2026-10-09 that trap was walked into: the superseded log was fed to the
# generator and the resulting parse failure was recorded as a new finding, when #165 had recorded
# both the failure and the forbidden-log warning three weeks earlier.
# SUPERSEDED TAKES ARE LISTED, NOT OMITTED. An absent file cannot warn anyone; a row marked
# superseded can. Anything reducing these cells must read the status column, not just glob the
#   1 cpu_model   the exact string gate-p5 greps, matching host-baselines.tsv and the README block
#   2 era         measurement-eras.tsv id; a cell pools only archives from its own era
#   3 rev         the keel rev the run was taken at
#   4 gate_log    the archived gate-p5 log, the artifact that NAMES the sample file
#   5 sample      the archived sample file, the artifact benchci actually reduces
#   7 arch        amd64 | arm64 (added 2026-10-28, #200): the GOARCH whose era the row is
#                 pooled under, since eras are scoped per architecture (§5 rule 17). Filled for
#                 the rows before it from the CPU model: every Neoverse-* string is arm64.
